newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong lawmakers endorse 1997/98 budget.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong lawmakers endorse 1997/98 budget.

text.p: Hong Kong lawmakers on Wednesday endorsed the 1997/98 budget, which straddles the territory's return to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.
The budget, covering the period from April 1, 1997, to March 31, 1998, passed with a vote of 30 for and 23 against.

Legislators who voted against it, mostly from the popular Democratic Party, were angry that the government refused to raise welfare payments to the elderly despite a surplus of HK$15.1 billion (US$1.96 billion) from the 1996/97 budget.
Financial Secretary Donald Tsang pledged to review the payment in 1998.

"We hope to be able to establish a rational basis for a revision. And my colleagues and I will certainly try our very best to find the resources for any justifiable increase in the coming year," Tsang told legislators.
